label: prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness
title: Uniqueness of the archimedean realization functor (Bloch-Suslin pentagon, conditional)
html:
Proposition (conditional on conj:dilogarithm-archimedean-limit and on the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991]). Let \tau_{\text{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau be the archimedean realization functor of the QOU substrate (archimedean realization functor), acting on motivic inputs assembled from braid / knot data. Under hypotheses (C1)–(C2) below, \tau_{\text{arch}} is uniquely determined, up to a single multiplicative real scalar, by the requirement that

  \lim_{q \to 1}\;\tau_{\text{arch}}\bigl(\Phi_q(z)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  D(z)
  \;:=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z|\,\arg(1-z)

equal the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm on every shape parameter z \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\}, where:

  • (C1) The substrate's mass-formula state sum is pentagon-coherent: \tau_{\text{arch}} is a continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued functional on B(\mathbb{C}) — the structural content provided by the cosimplicial / Yekutieli triple machinery (prop:cosimplicial-crossed-groupoid) together with the archimedean-limit class QOU.QPochhammer.ArchimedeanLimit (conj:dilogarithm-archimedean-limit).
  • (C2) Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness [suslin1991, bloch2000]: any continuous antisymmetric pentagon-coherent real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} is a constant scalar multiple of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm D.

The uniqueness reduces to the Bloch-Suslin pentagon characterisation: D is the unique (up to a real scalar) continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} satisfying the 5-term pentagon identity

  D(x) - D(y) + D\!\left(\tfrac{y}{x}\right)
  - D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y^{-1}}{1-x^{-1}}\right)
  + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y}{1-x}\right) \;=\; 0.

Theorem (conditional on conj:dilogarithm-archimedean-limit). The upstream conjecture is axiomatised in Lean as the typeclass QOU.QPochhammer.ArchimedeanLimit; the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991, bloch2000] is similarly axiomatised as QOU.Archimedean.BlochSuslinUniqueness. The Lean theorem QOU.Archimedean.archimedean_functor_uniqueness takes both classes as [Instance] hypotheses and is proved without sorry; the uniqueness statement therefore qualifies as a rigorous conditional result rather than an unproved conjecture.
